item.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to major prisoner swap as peace talks end
item.description:
The White House is "cautiously optimistic" as peace talks between Russia and Ukraine resume in Abu Dhabi this week, U.S. officials said on Monday. Why it matters: The talks on Tuesday and Wednesday will be the first time the parties have met with U.S. mediators present since February, when they were suspended due to the war in Iran. White House envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have worked for weeks to convince Russian President Vladimir Putin to restart negotiations. President Trump and his team hope Putin will be more willing to compromise after the U.S. lifted sanctions on Russian diesel sales and took other steps welcomed by Moscow. "The relations we have built with Putin will be instrumental in these negotiations," a U.S. official said. After the meetings in Abu Dhabi, Witkoff and Kushner may travel to Moscow and Kyiv to speak directly with Putin and Zelensky, a U.S. official…

item.title: General strike over housing brings out hundreds of thousands in Spain
item.description:
Workers in Spain held a general strike over the country’s housing affordability crisis, an issue that has swept to the top of voter concerns across Europe. Spain’s socialist leader hopes the demonstrations will galvanize support for his party ahead of elections this month. The housing crunch has worsened during his latest term, as it has across much of Europe: Renting a one-bedroom apartment in central Madrid costs about three-quarters of the average salary , with dozens of cities surpassing the 30% threshold generally considered optimal. Owning has gotten more expensive too as interest rates rise and persistent red tape makes new-home construction almost impossible. Demonstrators hope to seize on the moment. “ A historic window of opportunity has opened ,” one said. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

item.title: Hoax bomb threats target schools across Italy, UK and Ireland
item.description:
Francesco Fotia / Francesco Fotia/Reuters Schools in Europe were sent into a panic after bomb threats were made against thousands of them across the continent. Around 6,300 in Italy were evacuated after receiving bomb threats on Wednesday morning. “My daughter Dafne started crying because the kids did not understand what was happening, and she was still shaken when I picked her up,” said Nensi Bego, parent of a child at a school in Rome. Schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland also received a similar threat. However, the schools in the U.K. and Ireland deemed the threats to be a hoax, and no classes were disrupted. A previous hoax targeting hundreds of Scottish schools occurred in October. item.title: Jaylen Brown gives former teammate Jayson Tatum frosty greeting as Celtics beat 76ers
item.description:
The weightlessness of the early season and the ever-increasing rate of injuries can make it hard to sell a weeknight NBA game in November. There remains, however, a reliable shortcut between "box score I'll check in the morning" and "game I gotta watch live," and it is a route lined with beef. Beef was not promised in the leadup to Tuesday night's game between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers, which pit former teammates Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum against each other for the first time since Brown was traded in the offseason, but a savory aroma was in the air. item.title: Trump says the towering arch he wants to be build might be dedicated to military veterans
item.description:
On the 250th anniversary of the United States, as temperatures in Philadelphia climbed high enough to warp sneaker rubber, Michael McPhearson marched. The city had canceled its official parade due to extreme heat. But McPhearson, a 62-year-old Gulf War veteran, was undeterred. He had traveled across the country from Seattle to march alongside more than 500 of his fellow veterans, active-duty service members, and military families. They gathered near Independence Hall—America’s birthplace—but they didn’t come to commemorate a mythic nation untouched by contradiction. Instead, protesters stepped into the streets and unfurled a banner that read Veterans Against Fascism . The Fourth of July march was the largest anti-war veterans protest since the Vietnam War, according to organizers.
